summary: Gogebic County state fire tower on Copper Peak/Chippewa Hill: 80-ft steel tower staffed 1927-1943; the summit now has a 1969 ski-flying tower; fire tower fate not in sources.

facts.design: Steel fire tower, 80 ft (24.4 m), with a small house on top (1927 newspaper)

access.note: The summit is a visitor site built around the 1969 ski-jump tower; open Sundays in summer and fall during construction (Wikipedia). No source describes the fire tower site.

visit.trail_note: Chairlift to the landing, then an elevator up the ski-jump tower's 18 stories (copperpeak.net). This is the ski tower, not the 1927 fire tower.

events.note: Lone sentinel on watch in a little house on top of the 80-ft steel tower (August 1927 newspaper)
Blaze near the Triplett farm, Ironwood township, first seen by towerman Joseph Bergeron
Fire in Erwin township, Section 19, burning about 10 acres of slashing
Obituary of Joseph Bergeron: towerman for the state conservation department at the Chippewa hill fire tower for the past 10 years
Telephone line from the tower to the Black River county park completed by Camp Norrie enrollees; 5.5 miles long
Frank Cvengros named towerman in a June 1943 newspaper feature
Ski-flying hill built on the summit; inaugurated one year later
Designated a Michigan State Historic Site
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places
Michigan historical marker erected by the Michigan History Division, noting the 1845 copper tunnel

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Northern News Now calls the ski-jump tower 'the lookout from Copper Peak'. The story keeps it apart from the 80-ft fire tower: copperpeak.net gives the ski tower 18 stories, while the 1927 fire tower was 80 ft; the story gives both figures and makes no height comparison.

sources.title: Copper Peak (Aka Chippewa Hill), Forest Lookouts
Ski jump turned adventure ride gains state investment to return to old ways

notes_for_editor: Fate of the 1927 fire tower is not in any source read: the 1969 ski-flying hill is a separate structure, but nothing says whether the fire tower was removed for it. Brief coordinates 46.6006, -90.09 sit about 0.5 km north of Wikipedia (46.5964, -90.0906) and the HMDB marker (46.5987, -90.0884); check which point the fire tower stood on. The NRHP text is not digitized (npgallery). The Detroit News article returned 403 and was not used. The brief's status 'unknown' is left as is because no source says whether the fire tower stood or came down.
